subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: ARIA Roles and Attributes
description: A quick win: understand ARIA Roles and Attributes.

hook.text: A custom dropdown looks perfect visually. A screen reader announces it as just 'text.' It has no ARIA role.

buildup.text: ARIA adds roles, states, and properties to HTML elements so assistive technologies understand their purpose.

discovery.text: Role tells what it is. State tells its condition. Property provides extra context like labels or descriptions.

twist.text: The first rule of ARIA: don't use ARIA. If a native HTML element does the job, prefer it—it's more robust.

climax.text: Testing reveals ten custom components missing ARIA roles. Adding them makes each properly announced.

punchline.text: Use native HTML first. Add ARIA only when you must. Test both.

quiz.question: What is the first rule of ARIA?
options: Always use ARIA on every element
Don't use ARIA if a native HTML element works
